trust_decision.summary: All Olm/Megolm/SAS cryptography in nio is delegated to the third-party libolm library (python-olm); the advisory decides that nio must stop depending on it and run on vodozemac instead, and the fix re-implements every nio/crypto call site plus the on-disk pickle format, gated by the two package_installed("olm") import switches.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is only 'olm dependency deprecation'; the first thing an engineer checks is the declared dependency (python-olm in the e2e extra), then the runtime switch src/nio/crypto/__init__.py:23 and the first import olm at src/nio/crypto/sessions.py:21.

fix_sites.entry_point: import nio.crypto (sets ENCRYPTION_ENABLED and exports Olm/Sas/Session classes)
nio.crypto.Session / InboundSession / OutboundSession / InboundGroupSession (encrypt, decrypt, import_session)
nio.Client(...) with an encryption store: message encrypt/decrypt
Olm.decrypt -> Client.decrypt (session creation on pre-key message)
Olm.verify_signed_json (device key / cross-signing verification on sync)
from nio.store import DefaultStore, SqliteMemoryStore, MatrixStore

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The loader already falls back to libolm pickles, so rewriting the stored pickles into vodozemac format is only an optimisation - decryption keeps working if the store layer is left alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Accounts and sessions already persisted in libolm pickle format must keep loading with the same identity keys, so the fix deliberately keeps an olm fallback for pickle versions below 4 instead of removing libolm outright; a fix that simply stops importing olm logs existing users out of their encrypted rooms.

O6_input_shapes: account pickle: vodozemac format, libolm v4 format, and pre-v4 libolm format that only the olm package can re-pickle (fix.diff:598-627)
olm session pickle: vodozemac format and libolm v1 format (fix.diff:700-721)
inbound group session pickle: vodozemac format and libolm format (fix.diff:891-928)
outbound group session pickle: vodozemac format only (fix.diff:978-983)
ciphertext body: unpadded-base64 wire string vs raw bytes (fix.diff:88-99 and fix.diff:193-207)
olm message type 0 (pre-key) vs type 1 (normal) on decrypt (src/nio/crypto/olm_machine.py:1475-1485)
one-time-key count: full max_one_time_keys vs half of it (src/nio/crypto/olm_machine.py:275-276)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Shipped Docker image builds libolm from source (LIBOLM_VERSION=3.2.11) and copies libolm* into the runtime container, so deployments still carry the vulnerable library.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Docker/e2e build files, not library source; the advisory is about the Python dependency and the e2e extra.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: libolm build helper cloned and installed by the Dockerfile; nothing else in the tree installs libolm.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A shell helper for the e2e image; a solver can call it CI plumbing rather than code that reaches the crypto sink.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Arch Linux package recipe declares python-olm as a runtime dependency, so distro installs still pull libolm.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Third-party packaging recipe maintained separately; not built or tested by this project.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second pickle producer/consumer for OutboundGroupSession: it already carries rotation state (max_age, max_messages, message_count) but is never persisted at the pinned commit.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Persisting the outbound group session across restarts is an obvious follow-up, and the fix itself adds an OutboundGroupSession.from_pickle with no libolm branch (fix.diff:978-983), so the same format-migration check would be missing there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second store backend that pickles device keys or pending key requests, duplicating the load-time format upgrade.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: MatrixStore is a documented extension point (src/nio/store/__init__.py:9-11) with DefaultStore/SqliteStore/SqliteMemoryStore already subclassing it, so a maintainer adding a backend would copy the load_* pickling and could forget the vodozemac migration.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A passphrase-protected file serializer next to the sink, as an alternative to the sqlite pickle store.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already ships a second serialization boundary for encryption state (key export/import with PBKDF2), and a maintainer could move account or session blobs into that file, needing the same pickle-key derivation as derive_pickle_key.

O9_family: CWE-1395 dependency on a vulnerable third-party component: migration of the crypto backend from libolm/python-olm to vodozemac

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools / PEP 517 via pyproject.toml, pytest + tox (tox.ini:5-10); pinned commit needs the olm C library and python-olm built with cmake (docker/build_and_install_libolm.sh), the fix needs the vodozemac wheel instead
O10_build.project_tests: tests/encryption_test.py, tests/sessions_test.py, tests/sas_test.py, tests/store_test.py, tests/key_export_test.py - pytest against ephemeral sqlite stores and local test data, no network

j.j_sites_touched: pyproject.toml; src/nio/crypto/__init__.py; src/nio/crypto/olm_machine.py; src/nio/crypto/sas.py; src/nio/crypto/sessions.py; src/nio/store/__init__.py; src/nio/store/database.py
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Swap python-olm for vodozemac in the two import gates and pyproject.toml and port the obvious call sites, leaving stored libolm pickles unconverted and the store layer untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: CVE-2022-39255 and CVE-2024-45193 are flaws inside the third-party libolm C library, outside this repository; not examined.
unverified: repo_mb: directory size could not be measured without a shell; source tree is roughly 70 .py files so it is probably under 5 MB, which would be a tiny_repo red flag, but the threshold is unchecked.

O7 check_calls_producer: the fix's own new tests do read stored rows via DefaultStore._get_account (fix.diff:1174-1175, fix.diff:1280-1281), so a store-level check would call the producer; whether a hidden behavioural check does is unknown.
O8 present_in_latest: the input says the latest release for O8 is 'none', so presence of the docker/contrib routes in current code is unknown.

Whether vodozemac 0.9 exposes an equivalent for every libolm behaviour used here (e.g. the old hmac-sha256 SAS MAC, which the fix drops) was not checked, since no network or installed packages were used.
